request.spec:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Every change to a sheet now writes one line to the audit file, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How the server knows who made the change.** The signed-in user was only kept in the page URL, so the server had no way to tell who made a change. The person and claim forms now send the user as a `by` field with each add or edit (`features/people/people.slot.tsx`, `features/claims/claims.slot.tsx`). On the server, the new `session/ChangedBy.java` reads that field, and the existing validators pass it along. One side effect: a change sent with no user is now refused with "Sign in to make a change".

**Writing the lines.** Each of the four change endpoints has a new `audit` step just before it responds:
- `RecordPersonAdded` / `RecordPersonEdited` write `PERSON_ADDED` / `PERSON_EDITED … name=<name> grade=<grade>`.
- `RecordClaimAdded` / `RecordClaimEdited` write `CLAIM_ADDED` / `CLAIM_EDITED … person=<name> amount=<0.00> date=<yyyy-mm-dd>`. The shared format is in `claim/ClaimAudit.java`. For a claim edit, the person's current name is looked up from the claim.

**Refusals write nothing.** The audit step runs only after every check and the store write have succeeded. A refused change stops before it, so it neither changes data nor writes a line. A check added to these pipelines later will also leave nothing behind, as long as it goes before the `audit` step.

One small gap: the line is written just before the database commits. If the commit itself failed afterwards, a line would remain for a change that didn't happen. With the in-memory store that's very unlikely.
